thread:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: Alert: inference-runtime-us-east error_rate > 3% for 2m (triggered at 17:40 UTC). Page sent to #oncall-sre and #oncall-ml.

Ben Caldwell: acked. I'm oncall. looking now — starting mitigation plan.

Priya Singh: I see spike in 5xx across LLM-infer v2.3 shards in us-east-1, but us-west-2 looks healthy. error distribution shows KV cache thrash on long-context requests.

Alex Chen: customer-impact? any pay-tier customers affected?

Ben Caldwell: quick check: traffic routing shows ~12% of total tokens from us-east. Affected customers (by earliest trace ids): AcmePayments (high priority), HealthNLP Corp (sensitive), EduFlow (non-critical). Oncall-cs notified via DM.

Maya Rios: I'm going to temporarily enable region-failover to redirect new sessions from us-east -> us-west for the next 10m. Running command: 
```bash
redwood route set --from us-east-1 --to us-west-2 --filter 'model:llm-infer-v2' --duration 10m
```

Maya Rios: done — rule accepted, cluster shows gradual shift (~25% now).

Ben Caldwell: I'm scaling up replacement pool in us-east (dedicated pool autoscale didn't kick). Kicking off a rolling restart for the gc-heavy nodes to warm caches.

DeployBot: deploy job 84271 started by @Maya Rios. Rolling restart of infer-pool-us-east-3.

Priya Singh: noting alert noise: the current alert fires on short spikes (2m window). We should adjust to avoid flapping. Proposal: change `error_rate > 3% for 2m` -> `error_rate > 5% for 5m` OR keep 3% but require `error_count > 50` and `sustained 3m`. Thoughts?

Alex Chen: prefer requiring sustained signal + absolute error_count. We had alerts w/ tiny traffic buckets going noisy last month. Also let's add a composite alert that includes region latency and replica health so we don't page on small noisy errors.

Priya Singh: agree. Draft prometheus rule (quick):
```yaml
- alert: InferenceRegionHighError
  expr: sum(rate(inference_errors_total{region="us-east-1"}[1m])) / sum(rate(inference_requests_total{region="us-east-1"}[1m])) > 0.05
  for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    summary: "High inference error rate in us-east-1"
    runbook: "https://redwood.internal/runbooks/inference-region-high-error"
```

Jamie Ortiz: add a correlate condition: `and (sum by (region) (inference_latency_p50) > 200)` so we only page when both error and latency are bad. That reduces false positives.

Ben Caldwell: rolling restart finished. node health shows steady. error rate trending down to 1.1% now. Traffic shift to us-west peaked at 38% then stabilized ~22%.

Maya Rios: started a short-lived KV cache bypass for long sessions to prevent thrash: `config set infer.kv_cache.bypass_threshold=120s` — will revert after warmup.

Priya Singh: good. For post-incident: propose three followups:
- tune alert windows and add composite rule (Priya)
- new multi-region dashboard (Alex + Maya)
- failover alert when traffic shift > 30% within 2m or region outage detected (Jamie)

Alex Chen: add owners and deadlines.

Priya Singh: I'll open a PR with the new alert rules and update runbook. ETA EOD today. (link will be in the postmortem)

Maya Rios: I'll make a Grafana dashboard template: "Multi-region Inference Health" with panels: regional QPS, p50/p95 latency, error rate, replica_count, routing_shifts. ETA tomorrow morning.

Jamie Ortiz: I'll add a failover monitor rule to routing service: trigger if `traffic_shift >= 30%` AND `region_latency_p50 > 200ms` for 2m -> auto-notify oncall + kick routing fallback. I'll also add a synthetic probe for us-east endpoints (1m cadence). ETA 48h.

Ben Caldwell: customer comms: AcmePayments impacted for ~8 minutes at peak. CS sent templated note and flagged for SLO credit review. HealthNLP saw degraded latency but no data loss. I'll collect traces and attach to incident thread.

Incident Bot: Incident acknowledged by Ben Caldwell, severity: Sev 2 -> downgraded to Sev 3 at 17:58 UTC (error rate under 2% and routing stable).

Alex Chen: good call. Add these to the incident action tracker. Also require adding the new composite alert to the Dedicated customers' monitoring so enterprise customers don't get noisy pages.

Priya Singh: notes for postmortem: root cause likely an interaction between KV cache eviction & a memory pressure GC cycle on a subset of us-east nodes; exacerbated by bursty long-context sessions from AcmePayments. We'll include replay of request patterns.

Maya Rios: I'll keep the temporary route rule for another 5m then revert. Reversion command: `redwood route delete --id <temp-id>` — I'll post ID when it's up.

Ben Caldwell: thanks all. I'll compile the incident timeline and open the postmortem doc later today. Action items:
- Priya: PR for alert tuning + runbook update (due: today EOD)
- Maya: Grafana dashboard + temp route clean-up (due: tomorrow 10:00 UTC)
- Jamie: routing failover monitor + synthetic probe (due: in 48h)
- Ben: postmortem + traces + customer impact summary (due: today EOD)

Alex Chen: @channel please react with :thumbsup: when you've captured the action item in your task tracker. We'll do a quick follow-up sync tomorrow 09:30 UTC to review dashboards and alert changes.

DeployBot: deploy job 84271 succeeded. Rolling restart completed at 17:53 UTC.

Ben Caldwell: closing—monitoring for 30m then I'll unassign. Thanks team. :heart:
